IsPlayable.issue: The PREDICATE is faithful -- `CardPile.GetCards(Owner, PileType.Hand).All(c => c.Type == CardType.Attack)` (Clash.cs:20) == `all(c.card_type == CardType.ATTACK for c in self.combat.player.hand)`, and the sim correctly returns True for every other card so the listener only vetoes itself. THE HOOK IS WRONG. C# `IsPlayable` is consulted in exactly ONE place: `CardModel.CanPlay` (CardModel.cs:1759-1762, `if (!IsPlayable) reason |= UnplayableReason.BlockedByCardLogic`), which is the MANUAL play path. `CardCmd.AutoPlay` does not call CanPlay -- it checks only the Unplayable KEYWORD and `Hook.ShouldPlay` (CardCmd.cs:57-71), and Clash implements neither. So in the game an AUTO-PLAYED Clash fires regardless of what else is in hand. The sim routes the gate through `should_play_card`, which `CombatState.auto_play_card` DOES consult (combat.py:536, with `auto_play=True`), and Clash's implementation ignores that flag -- so the sim moves Clash to the discard pile without playing it. Observable: a mixed hand plus any auto-play source -- the game deals 14, the sim deals 0. LIVE: Clash is a ported Event Attack (Trash Heap) and four ported cards auto-play Attacks from a pile -- card/beat_down (Attacks from the discard pile), card/havoc, card/catastrophe and card/cascade (top of the draw pile) -- plus relics/events that auto-play. The fix shape is `if auto_play: return True`.

ShouldGlowGoldInternal.rationale: `protected override bool ShouldGlowGoldInternal => IsPlayable` (Clash.cs:22) is the golden-glow highlight in the hand UI. Presentation, out of scope, and the sim has no card-visual layer.
